subject: StorixAI renewal: staged commit + scale incentive
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@storix.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal and growth incentives

Samir —

Following our Q1 usage check-in, Storix is tracking a sustained increase in inference volume (avg tokens/day +180% QoQ). Based on that, I'd like to propose a renewal structure that aligns cost with predictable capacity while unlocking a concession package for scale. High level: 

- Term: 12 months (Jul 1 start)
- Commit: 2.5x current committed units (staged start, see MAAP option below)
- Unit price: 12% discount vs current list for committed tokens
- Credits: $30k platform credit applied to onboarding and initial ramp over first 90 days
- Price hold: locked for first 6 months after start; after that we offer true-up/quarterly reprice guard language
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for production routes included

Two optional protections to consider: a) staged commit (ramp in months 1–3 at 60% of full commit, then step to full), or b) flat commit with a lighter discount but deeper immediate credits. Both help procurement cashflow while giving you capacity headroom.

Attached: Storix_Monthly_Usage_Q1.pdf (usage snapshot). If this looks in the right direction, I can loop in Naomi (CS) and Marissa (Legal) to draft a simple MAAP + draft amendment.

Next steps: are you free for a 30-min call Wed or Thu to walk through the options and get procurement asks?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Vivek —

Appreciate the thoughtful proposal. A couple quick points from our side:

- We like the staged-commit idea; biggest ask is to avoid a large upfront invoice if we under-index on usage in month 1–2.
- Procurement will push for net-30 and a simpler invoice cadence (monthly preferred).
- Can you confirm the mechanics of the $30k credit (applied to invoices vs one-time offset)? We prefer invoice credits.
- We also need SOC2 + data handling summary (security team flagged that) before legal moves fast.

If you can do a variant with a lower initial commit (1.2x) that auto-steps to 2.5x by month 4 based on thresholds, that would help us. Also please include a quarterly true-up (not monthly).

I'm copying procurement to surface any PO timing constraints. Happy to jump on a call Thu 11am PT.

Best,

Option A — Staged step-up (preferred for Storix)
- Months 1–3: 1.2x existing commit
- Month 4 onward: automatic step to 2.5x if 3-month rolling usage >= 90% of target; if not, we keep 1.2x and revisit at the next quarterly true-up
- Discount: 12% off list on committed usage once at 2.5x (pro-rated during staged months)
- Credits: $30k invoice credit (applied evenly over months 1–3)
- Price hold: no unit price increase for first 6 months after effective date
- Billing: monthly invoices with quarterly true-up (preferred by you)

Option B — Immediate commit, smaller discount
- Commit: 2.5x from day one
- Discount: 8% off list
- Credits: $50k one-time credit applied to first invoice
- Price hold: 3 months

Security/Docs: attaching SOC2 summary and a draft MAAP that maps milestones and verification gates. Naomi — can you confirm operational onboarding timeline (we're proposing a 4-week migrate + smoke test plan)? Marissa/Ben — we'll need a short contract amendment and payment term note (Samir prefers net-30).

If Thu 11am PT works, I'll book and include Naomi to walk technical onboarding.

Subject: Fwd: Storix renewal — contract redline items

Forwarding our internal redline notes after reviewing the MAAP and proposed commercial terms. High-level asks for negotiation: 

1) No automatic evergreen renewals — require mutual signed amendment to renew (customer prefers automatic renewals; we should trade for a longer initial term or a larger credit).
2) Credit expiry: credits must expire within 90 days unless specifically reserved for onboarding milestones; procurement will want longer — propose a 6-month carveout for onboarding only.
3) Limitation of liability carve: keep standard Redwood language but add an operations SLA credit mechanism (not cash).
4) True-up window: contractually limit price adjustments to quarterly reconciliations with 30 days notice.

I've attached a redline with in-line comments (contract_redline_storix.docx). Ben — can you confirm the invoice-credit flow (how credits reduce monthly invoices vs issuing a separate credit memo)?
